title: PossibleCooker White Chicken Chili with Green Chile Gravy
description: Tender thigh pieces and white beans simmer in a mild roasted green chile gravy finished with whipped cream cheese.
equipment: Immersion blender and deep heatproof jug

ingredients.name: boneless skinless chicken thighs
ingredients.note: Trim fat and cut across the grain into 3/4-inch pieces.

ingredients.name: low-sodium chicken broth
ingredients.note: Choose plain meat-and-bone broth without a vegetable blend.

ingredients.name: peeled roasted mild green chile
ingredients.note: Mild Anaheim, seeds and ribs removed; use plain, unsalted peppers.

steps.title: Blend the bean base
steps.text: Blend half of {beans} with {chile} and enough {broth} to make a smooth puree in a deep jug.

steps.title: Heat the chili base
steps.text: Pour the puree, remaining {broth}, {garlic}, {cumin} and {oregano} into the PossibleCooker. Select Sear/Sauté HIGH, leave the lid off and stir until the base begins to simmer, about 5–8 minutes.

steps.title: Poach the chicken
steps.text: Add {chicken} and the remaining {beans}. Once the liquid returns to a simmer, change to Sear/Sauté LOW. Cook uncovered at a gentle bubble for 12–18 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the largest chicken pieces reach 175°F.

steps.title: Mix the slurry
steps.text: Stir {starch} into {water} in a small cup until smooth.

steps.title: Thicken the chili
steps.text: Stir the slurry into the bubbling chili and cook for 1 minute until the white gravy coats the back of a spoon. Use HIGH briefly if needed to restore the simmer, then turn the cooker off.

steps.title: Finish the bowls
steps.text: Loosen {cheese} with a spoonful of hot chili and fold back into the pot until smooth. Ladle generous amounts of white gravy over the chicken in each bowl.

notes: Make ahead: Puree the beans and pepper a day ahead and refrigerate the base separately from the raw chicken. Option A uses mild green chile. For gentler Option B, use peeled roasted sweet green bell pepper instead and halve the cumin. For dairy-free chili leave out the cream cheese; the bean puree and slurry give the gravy body. Refrigerate promptly in shallow portions and use within 3 days. Freezer-Friendly Verdict: Yes. Freeze the chili without cream cheese for up to 2 months and stir it in after reheating. Fridge reheat: Warm a single portion with its sauce in a covered HexClad skillet over medium-low, adding a splash of water if thick. Stir or turn gently and begin checking after 5 minutes. Heat the chicken to 165°F throughout. Freezer reheat: Thaw overnight in the refrigerator. Use the fridge reheating directions and stir the sauce smooth. Estimated nutrition per serving (1/4 of recipe): 318 kcal, 35.9 g protein, 26.7 g total carbohydrate, 7.2 g fat, 5.9 g fiber, 172 mg sodium. Includes the measured broth and sauce. Sodium varies with your broth.
